memory_candidates.content: When sweeping a repo for orphans left by a targeted deletion, reachability analysis (index-entries.json/index.json rows resolving to files on disk, load_when bindings) and glob/pattern-prose auditing (grepping for the deleted artifact's name expanded with wildcards, e.g. 'skill-team' not just the three literal skill names) catch disjoint defect classes. A file can be perfectly 'reachable' (valid index row, matching load_when.agents binding) while its content is entirely dead, because load_when governs injection mechanics, not content correctness. Reachability tooling (e.g. check-extension-docs.sh's line_count/undeclared-file checks) will report a fully clean tree while missing this; only reading files found via the pattern-prose grep catches it.

This repo recycles task numbers across vault-archival epochs, so `git log --grep="task N"` or `git log --oneline | grep "task N"` can silently mix commits from unrelated tasks that happened to reuse the same number in an earlier epoch. To scope a git history search to one specific task's actual work, anchor on a known commit hash from that task (e.g. its creation commit) and use a commit-range diff (`git log --diff-filter=D ... <anchor>..HEAD`) rather than grepping commit messages by task number alone.
